Bounds/source queries and hit testing retain controlled work charging and cancellation. The port preserves reverse painter order, fill rules, clip calls, inverse-space stroke distance, tolerance scaling, source specificity and append-time source assignment. Real sealed-graph fixtures exercise the accepted path, animation and lexical APIs.

Query allocations now use the accepted `ChargeLedger::allocate_buffer` and opaque `LedgerBuffer` API inside a scope-owned `TrackedBuffer`. Exact `LedgerIdentity` and source ownership are checked through `require_owner`; no mutable Vec, lease, or zero-byte probe escapes. Replacement counts its overlap record against the 65,536 cap, uses shared requested-byte preallocation and actual-capacity reconciliation, then lets the accepted buffer operation drop/release old storage. Typed zero initialization is performed after admission without an unaccounted temporary. Tests cover same-source wrong-ledger, wrong source/tracker, stale/double release, cap boundary/bypass, old/new peak and release, budget rejection, native reserve failure, arithmetic, and cancellation cleanup. Successful physical allocations and metadata history remain recorded after cancellation.

The original pure fixture builder assertions pass. The mixed `measure_allocation_source` inputs and assertions remain preserved but unexecuted pending concrete decoder/reference-index, clip-copy and raster-output composition. Full renderer/app/runtime/release/authentic MCP demo and product QA remain later gates. This is a candidate pending independent root review and fresh main checks.

# Scene queries and allocation admission

This crate ports safe scene selection and explicit memory-capacity accounting.
`bounds_query` and `hit_test` consume immutable accepted `SceneView` data;
hit testing requires the real `KernelResources` clip implementation and a
caller work controller. Controlled bounds/source variants and hit testing
charge visited edges/shapes and observe cancellation. `element_at_offset`
selects the narrowest half-open source span, with later painter order winning
ties. Slot enumeration uses accepted `SceneView::shape_id`, including
zero-edge shapes, and inherits its generation/scene/owner validation.

Scene publication assigns source spans on `ShapeInput` before
`SceneBuilder::append_shape`. `source_assign` therefore modifies only an
unpublished input; published spans remain immutable. Shapes are reached with
accepted generation-checked handles. Query storage uses the accepted
`ChargeLedger::allocate_buffer` and opaque `LedgerBuffer`, wrapped in a
scope-owned `TrackedBuffer`; no Vec or lease escapes. `LedgerIdentity` and
`require_owner` bind each operation to the same source and exact ledger.
`reserve_table` uses the accepted replacement operation, which admits requested
bytes before physical reservation and reconciles actual capacity before
publication. Old and new lease records overlap until the old storage is dropped.
`track_filled_buffer` applies typed zero initialization after admission without
allocating an unaccounted temporary buffer.
Cancellation releases temporary live capacity while retaining successful
physical allocation history and honest ledger metadata. The adapter applies the
legacy 65,536 record bound to initial buffers and replacement overlap. It does
not claim raw allocator hooks, allocator metadata, or RSS.

The mixed original measurement fixture still requires coordinator composition
with the concrete decoder/reference index, clip-copy producer, and raster
output. Those integration assertions are retained in the work-order coverage
record; they are not claimed as passed here.

**ACCEPT — full owned source scope only.** The current crate maps all 22 catalog symbols: eight selection symbols and fourteen allocation symbols, including documented safe adaptations. The Rust implementation and tests cover zero-edge shape IDs, stale and foreign handles, painter order, fill and stroke behavior, clipping, source-span selection and append-time assignment, bounds mapping, and tolerance checks. Allocation coverage includes exact ledger and source ownership, stale and duplicate release rejection, the 65,536-record cap including replacement overlap, actual capacity accounting, budget and arithmetic failures, and cancellation cleanup.

I found no unaccounted mutable `Vec` or lease escape, available-only allocation preflight, skipped pure helper, or source/test file over 800 lines. The recorded scoped check, test, and work-order validation evidence is consistent with the artifacts; I did not rerun them.

Later gates remain: the original `measure_allocation_source` decode/render assertions need concrete decoder/reference-index, clip-copy, and raster-output composition. Full renderer, app/runtime, native-provider, and product QA integration also remain unclaimed.
